subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: Should OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests within one reviewer/run, and what exact cache lifetime, key, and cached outcomes are approved?
rationale: The current behavior is source-reproducible and wasteful, but caching a model-backed exec approval reviewer result changes one-request-one-review semantics on a security-sensitive path.

options.title: Approve bounded exact-input memo
options.body: Cache only within one reviewer/run using the full reviewed input or prompt as the key, with a small bound, key-separation coverage, and no durable approval reuse.

options.title: Narrow to low-risk allows only
options.body: Memoize only parsed low-risk `allow-once` outcomes and keep ask, error, and timeout results uncached for a smaller approval-boundary change.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Reject reviewer-result caching for now and accept repeated model cost until a different cost-control design is approved.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded exact-input memo
recommendation.body: Cache only within one reviewer/run using the full reviewed input or prompt as the key, with a small bound, key-separation coverage, and no durable approval reuse.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle introduced the normalized auto-mode reviewer surface and is the clearest feature-history owner for approving the cache boundary.
